full.description: This image is a schematic diagram illustrating the pathophysiology of hereditary spherocytosis. It depicts a normal red blood cell on the left, a cross-section of the RBC membrane showing molecular abnormalities in spectrin-ankyrin interactions, a resultant microspherocyte, and phagocytosis of the abnormal RBC by macrophages in the spleen. The most likely diagnosis represented is hereditary spherocytosis.

random.description: This image is a diagram illustrating the pathophysiology of hereditary spherocytosis affecting red blood cells. It shows a normal red blood cell and a cross-section of an erythrocyte membrane with molecular defects leading to membrane instability. The cell loses surface area and becomes a microspherocyte. These abnormal cells undergo increased destruction (hemolysis) in the spleen.
